chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazal, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Ibn Abu Yafour who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Baziya alleges that he is a Prophet.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'If you were to hear him saying that, kill him.' He said, 'So I sat with him (awaiting) many a time, but was not able to do so.'

key_terms.بَزِيعاً: A specific individual known for claiming prophethood
key_terms.غَيْرَ مَرَّةٍ: More than once / many a time

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for someone who claims to be a prophet in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes the ruling for a person who claims prophethood, with the Imam (peace be upon him) instructing that if one hears such a person explicitly making this claim, they should be killed. The narrator confirms the instruction by noting he waited for the claimant to speak but did not hear the specific declaration. In Shia jurisprudence, this is often linked to the concept of *al-Murtadd al-Mutlaq* (absolute apostate), where the claim of prophethood after Muhammad (peace be upon him and his progeny) is considered a definitive rejection of Islam, warranting immediate execution upon verified testimony.
